You are reverse-engineering a Python program so it can be reimplemented in JavaScript. The program is at /workspace/dataset/test13_executable. Its source is: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Markdown with extension configuration") parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True) parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True) parser.add_argument('--c', type=str, required=True) args = parser.parse_args() html1 = markdown.markdown(args.a, extensions=['extra', 'tables']) html2 = markdown.markdown(args.b, extensions=['codehilite']) html3 = markdown.markdown(args.c, extensions=['fenced_code', 'toc']) combined = markdown.markdown(f"{html1}\n{html2}\n{html3}") print(html1); print(html2); print(html3); print(combined) So: --a is parsed with extensions [extra, tables]; --b with [codehilite]; --c with [fenced_code, toc]; and the concatenation is re-parsed with NO extensions. HOW TO RUN PROBES (bash). Use $'...' quoting so \n becomes a real newline: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a $'line1\nline2' --b 'x' --c 'y' To isolate one channel, put a trivial marker in the other two, e.g. --b 'B' --c 'C'. To see exact bytes including trailing whitespace, pipe through: | cat -A (or | od -c for tricky cases) Run MANY probes. Batch several probes per bash call with echo separators so you use few tools calls. Never use the 'python' command. Only run the executable. YOUR OUTPUT is a technical spec fragment, not prose for a human. For every behavior you establish, give the exact input and the exact output bytes. Be precise about: leading/trailing newlines, whether blocks are separated by a blank line, exact attribute order and quoting, exact whitespace inside tags. Report SURPRISES loudly — cases where the output is not what a CommonMark implementation would produce. Do NOT speculate; if you did not run it, do not claim it. Aim for a dense, complete, correct report. AREA: tables (extension) and blockquotes. --a has 'extra'+'tables' so tables work there. --b and --c do NOT have tables. Verify that. Establish: 1. Minimal table: '| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |' -> exact full HTML bytes (, , , ,
,
) with exact indentation and newlines. This must be byte exact. 2. Table without leading/trailing pipes. Table with alignment rows ':---', '---:', ':---:', mixed. Exact style attribute output (e.g. 'style="text-align: left;"') and its position in the tag. 3. Ragged rows (fewer/more cells than header). Empty cells. Cell containing inline markdown (*em*, code span, link). Cell containing an escaped pipe '\|' and a pipe inside a code span. 4. A table not preceded by a blank line; a table immediately after a paragraph. 5. Same table input through --b and --c: show it renders as a paragraph instead, with exact escaping of '|'. 6. Blockquotes: '> a', multi-line, lazy continuation, nested '> > b', blockquote containing a list, a heading, a code block, a fenced block. '>' with no space, '>' alone, blank '>' lines separating paragraphs. Exact output layout ('
\n

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

# SPEC FRAGMENT — tables + blockquotes (`/workspace/dataset/test13_executable`) Source confirmed at `/workspace/dataset/test13.py` (matches the brief). Engine is **Python-Markdown 3.x**, not CommonMark. ## 0. Output framing (byte-exact) Each of the 4 `print()` calls emits `html` + `\n`. `markdown.markdown()` returns text with **no** trailing newline and **no** blank line between top-level blocks. Whole-stdout od for `--a '| a |\n|---|\n| 1 |' --b B --c C`: ``` \n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n
a
1
\n

B

\n

C

\n…
\n

B

\n

C

\n ``` Empty `--a` → `html1 == ""`, so stdout starts with a bare `\n`; the combined pass then yields `

B

\n

C

` with no leading blank (input `"\n

B

\n

C

"`). Combined (no-extension) pass: all block-level HTML emitted by passes 1–3 (`…`, `
…`, `

…

`) is preserved **verbatim** as raw-HTML blocks. Every probe below round-trips identically through `combined`. --- ## 1. Tables — only in `--a` ### 1.1 Canonical layout, zero indentation Input `--a`: `| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |` ```
a b
1 2
``` No leading spaces on any line; newline after every tag; no newline inside ``/``. ### 1.2 Recognition rules (probed) | input | result | |---|---| | `a \| b` / `--- \| ---` / `1 \| 2` (no outer pipes) | table, identical to 1.1 | | leading pipe only (`\| a \| b` / `\|---\|---`) | table | | trailing pipe only (`a \| b \|` / `---\|---\|`) | table | | 2-space indent on all 3 lines | table | | header cells (3) > delimiter cells (2) | **NOT a table** → one `

` | | delimiter cells (3) > header cells (2) | **NOT a table** → one `

` | | header line with no `\|` (`a b` / `---\|---`) | **NOT a table** | | delimiter `\|===\|===\|` | **NOT a table** | | delimiter `\|--x--\|---\|` | **NOT a table** | | delimiter `\|-\|-\|` (1 dash) | table | | delimiter `\| : \| : \|` (colon only, no dash) | table, both **center** | | delimiter `\|::\|---\|` | table, col1 **center** | | delimiter `\|:-\|-:\|` | left / right | | missing delimiter row entirely | `

` | Column count is `len(align)` from the delimiter row and is authoritative. ### 1.3 Alignment `| a | b | c | d |` / `|:---|---:|:---:|---|` / `| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |` ``` a b c d … 1 2 3 4 ``` Exact attribute text: `style="text-align: left;"` — space after colon, trailing semicolon, double quotes. It is the **only** attribute, placed directly after the tag name. Unaligned columns emit the bare tag with no `style`. Whitespace inside the delimiter cell is ignored (`| --- |`, `| :------ | ------: |` behave the same). ### 1.4 Ragged rows / empty cells - Fewer cells than header → missing `` are appended **empty but WITH the column's style**: `| a | b | c |` / `|:--|--:|:-:|` / `| 1 | 2 |` → `1`, `2`, ``. - More cells than header → **extra cells silently dropped**: `| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |` with 3 columns → exactly 3 ``. Same for `| 1 | 2 | |` with 2 columns. - Row that is just `|` → full row of empty ``. - Empty header cell → ``; `|| b |` → `b`. ### 1.5 SURPRISE — header-only table still emits a body row `| a | b |\n|---|---|` (no data rows) → ``` ``` and with alignment `|:--|--:|` the synthesized empty row's cells carry **no `style` attribute** — `` — unlike the ragged-fill cells in 1.4 which do. (Two different code paths.) ### 1.6 Cell content / escaping - Inline markdown works: `em`, `co|de`, `l`. - Pipes inside **backtick code spans do not split cells**: `` | `x | y` | 2 | `` → `x | y2`. - **SURPRISE** — pipes inside a link destination **do** split: `| [l](u|v) | 2 |` → `[l](uv)` (3rd cell dropped). Only backticks protect. - `\|` splits nothing and renders as `|`: `| x \| y | 2 |` → `x | y`. Works in the header row too: `| a \| z | b |` → `a | z`. - `\\|` → backslash is consumed as an escaped backslash and the pipe **does** split: `| x \\| y | 2 |` → `x \y`. - Inside a code span the backslash is **not** removed: `` | `x \| y` | `` → `x \| y`. - Raw HTML passes through: `x`. Text escaping: input `& & < > "` → `& & < > "` (`"` left bare). - `\*x\*` → `*x*`; `\\` → `\`. - Leading/trailing spaces and tabs around cell text are stripped; trailing whitespace on the whole line is ignored. ### 1.7 SURPRISE — `\|` becomes a document-wide escape in `--a` The `tables` extension appends `|` to the escaped-character set for that whole conversion: - `--a 'x \| y'` (plain paragraph, no table anywhere) → `

x | y

` - `--b 'x \| y'` and `--c 'x \| y'` → `

x \| y

` (backslash retained) ### 1.8 Block boundaries — SURPRISES - **Paragraph immediately before a table kills the table.** `Hello\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |` → a single `

Hello\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |

`. - **Any non-blank line immediately after a table becomes a table row.** - `…| 1 | 2 |\nHello` → extra `Hello` - `…| 1 | 2 |\n# H` → `# H` - `|---|---|\n> q` → `> q` Only a blank line terminates the table. - A **heading** immediately before a table is fine: `# H\n| a |…` → `

H

` then the table. - A **list** immediately before swallows it: `- x\n| a | b |…` → `
  • x\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |
